mainTopic: The end of the story of שמואל and the nests of לוי בר סימון, the משנה forbidding taking the mother bird even for a מצוה, and רבי יעקב's teaching that the Torah's promised rewards are paid in עולם הבא.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. Why did שמואל have someone bang on the nest, when simply saying 'this and that I will take' should have been enough? The answer is that the eggs were newly laid and the mothers had never risen off them, so לוי בר סימון did not own them yet. They had to be acquired first and then handed over with a סודר. Next comes a new משנה: you may not take the mother bird with her young, even to purify a מצורע. The משנה adds a קל וחומר: if this cheap, easy מצוה earns a good and long life, harder מצוות surely earn at least as much. In the גמרא, רבי יעקב teaches that these written rewards are really given after תחיית המתים. He proves it from a son who kept both כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן and then fell and died. The גמרא defends this proof against several challenges: maybe it never happened, maybe he had sinful thoughts, and maybe שלוחי מצוה are protected from harm. It ends with the answer that the son was on a shaky ladder, a place of known danger. רב יוסף then says that אחר would not have lost his faith had he read the פסוק like רבי יעקב, his grandson, and the מסכת closes with the הדרן.

steps.title: Why bang on the nest when designating should be enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: just standing and saying 'this and that I will take' should have been enough, so why did שמואל require banging on the nest?
steps.simpleTranslation: Just standing (before יום טוב) and saying 'This one and that one I will take' is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a question from the earlier discussion. It asks why שמואל needed a special act with the nest, when a simple verbal designation should have worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes the birds already belonged to לוי בר סימון. If they did, only a simple designation would be needed, and the instruction to bang on the nest would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This one and that one I will take', a verbal designation of birds for later use
It is enough

phrases.english: By standing and saying
'This one and that one I will take' is enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹמֵד וְאוֹמֵר ״זֶה וְזֶה אֲנִי נוֹטֵל״ סַגִּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's instruction to bang on the nest.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple designation would be enough, so the extra act looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The eggs were new and not yet owned
steps.stepSummary: The eggs were newly laid and the mothers had never risen off them, so לוי בר סימון did not own them yet. Banging on the nest made the mothers rise, his courtyard acquired the eggs, and then he could give them over with a סודר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those eggs were new produce that לוי בר סימון himself had not yet acquired. So this is what שמואל meant: go bang on the nest so the mothers rise up. Then לוי בר סימון will acquire the eggs, and afterward he can transfer them to you with a cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Designation alone was not enough because the owner did not own the new eggs yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the eggs already belonged to לוי בר סימון. The answer shows the real problem was ownership, not designation. A courtyard cannot acquire eggs while the mother is sitting on them (Rashi). Once the mothers rise off the nest, his courtyard acquires the eggs, and then he can pass them on through קנין סודר.

keyTerms.meaning: New produce, here newly laid eggs the mother never rose off
Bang on the nest
Acquires, takes legal ownership
A cloth used to transfer ownership (קנין סודר)

steps.whatToRemember: The extra step was needed because of ownership: new eggs had to be acquired before they could be given away.

phrases.english: Those were new produce,
phrases.notes: 'New produce' here means newly laid eggs that the mother had never risen off (Rashi).

phrases.english: which Levi bar Simon himself
had not acquired,
and this is what he was saying to him:
Go and bang on the nest,
so that they rise up,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the mother birds lifting off the nest.

phrases.english: and Levi bar Simon will acquire them,
and then he can transfer them to you with a cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the birds were not yet owned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The birds already belonged to לוי בר סימון, so a simple designation would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eggs were new and unowned. They had to be acquired first and then transferred with a סודר.

steps.title: Do not take the mother with the young, even for a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may not take the mother bird together with her young, even to use her for purifying a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not take the mother bird with the young, even to purify a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the ban on taking the mother bird stays in force even when the bird is needed for another מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a different מצוה, like purifying a מצורע, would allow taking the mother bird. The משנה says no: the obligation of שילוח הקן still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The mother bird together with her young
A person with צרעת, whose purification uses birds

phrases.english: Mishnah

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִטּוֹל אָדָם אֵם עַל בָּנִים,
phrases.english: A person may not take the mother with the young,
even to purify the metzora.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִטּוֹל אָדָם אֵם עַל בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the mother with the young is forbidden, even for the מצוה of purifying a מצורע.

steps.title: A קל וחומר about the reward for מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reasons that if an easy, cheap מצוה earns a good and long life, then the harder מצוות surely earn at least as much.
steps.simpleTranslation: If for an easy מצוה, which costs only about an איסר, the Torah says 'so that it will be good for you and you will lengthen your days', then all the more so for the weighty מצוות of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה praises the reward for מצוות using a קל וחומר, starting from שילוח הקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שילוח הקן costs almost nothing, only the value of one bird. Yet the Torah promises it a great reward. So harder, costlier מצוות must earn a reward at least that great.

keyTerms.meaning: An easy, light מצוה
A small coin of little value
An argument from lesser to greater
Weighty, demanding מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה uses שילוח הקן to show how great the reward for every מצוה is.

phrases.english: And if regarding an easy מצוה,
which is like an issar,
phrases.notes: An issar is a small coin, which is about what the mother bird is worth.

phrases.english: the Torah said
'So that it will be good for you and you will lengthen your days,'

phrases.aramaic: קַל וָחוֹמֶר עַל מִצְוֹת חֲמוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: then all the more so for the weighty מצוות of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a teaching about reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If an easy מצוה earns a long, good life, harder מצוות earn at least as much.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: written rewards depend on תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב teaches that every reward written next to a מצוה in the Torah is really fulfilled through תחיית המתים. His examples are כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: there is no מצוה in the Torah whose reward is written next to it that does not depend on תחיית המתים. About honoring father and mother it says 'so that your days will be long and so that it will be good for you'. About sending away the nest it says 'so that it will be good for you and you will lengthen your days'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי יעקב. He says the Torah's promised rewards are paid in the world after תחיית המתים, and he names two מצוות that promise long life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב makes a sweeping claim about every reward written in the Torah. He chooses the two מצוות that promise long and good days, which sets up the proof that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Its reward is written right next to it
The resurrection of the dead
Honoring father and mother
Sending away the mother bird from the nest

phrases.english: Gemara
It was taught: Rabbi Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל מִצְוָה וּמִצְוָה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: There is not a single מצוה in the Torah
whose reward is written next to it,
that does not depend on the resurrection of the dead.
phrases.notes: He means the promised reward is really given after תחיית המתים, not in this world.

phrases.english: Regarding honoring father and mother it is written:
'So that your days will be long and so that it will be good for you,'
Regarding sending away the nest it is written:
'So that it will be good for you and you will lengthen your days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reward mentioned in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rewards written next to מצוות are fulfilled through תחיית המתים, as with כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן.

steps.title: The son who did both מצוות and died
steps.stepSummary: A son obeys his father, climbs up, sends away the mother bird, and takes the young. He falls and dies on the way back. So where are his promised long and good days?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a case: a father told his son, 'Go up to the building and bring me chicks.' He went up, sent away the mother, and took the young. On the way back he fell and died. Where is this one's long life? And where is this one's goodness?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב brings a case to prove his point. The case shows that the reward cannot be about this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son did both of the מצוות that promise long life, at the very same moment, yet he died right away. So the promise cannot mean a long life in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: A building, a tall structure
Young birds, chicks
Length of days, a long life

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as questioning whether the Torah's promise is true. The point is that the promise is real, but it refers to עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Here is a case where his father said to him:
Go up to the building and bring me chicks!
And he went up, and sent away the mother
and took the young,
and on his way back he fell and died.
Where is this one's length of days?
And where is this one's goodness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יעקב's claim with a real-life case.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah's promised reward is not paid in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A son who did both כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן and died immediately.

steps.title: The reward is in the world that is entirely long and good
steps.stepSummary: So the verses must mean long days in the world that is entirely long, and goodness in the world that is entirely good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'so that your days will be long' means in the world that is entirely long, and 'so that it will be good for you' means in the world that is entirely good.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב concludes how to read the verses: the promised reward is in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this-world long life cannot be what the verses mean, he reads each phrase as pointing to עולם הבא. That world is endless ('entirely long') and completely good.

keyTerms.meaning: The world that is entirely long, meaning עולם הבא
The world that is entirely good

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יעקב, the Torah's promises of long and good days are fulfilled in עולם הבא, not necessarily in this world.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that the reward for מצוות is mainly in עולם הבא (שכר מצוה בהאי עלמא ליכא).

phrases.english: Rather, 'so that your days will be long' —
in the world that is entirely long,
and 'so that it will be good for you' —
in the world that is entirely good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the case in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The promised long and good days refer to עולם הבא, the world that is entirely long and entirely good.

steps.title: Maybe the story never happened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יעקב's story of the son who fell and died may be only a made-up case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it never happened like that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יעקב's proof. Maybe nobody who did these מצוות ever actually died like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's whole proof rests on a real case where the promised reward did not come in this world. If that case is only imagined, the proof falls away, and we could say the reward does come in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe; introduces a possible weakness in the argument
It did not happen this way

phrases.english: But perhaps it never happened this way?
phrases.notes: He means the story in step 6, the son who fell and died on his way back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the factual basis of the proof in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The reality of the case in רבי יעקב's proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A made-up case cannot prove that reward is not given in this world

steps.title: רבי יעקב saw it happen himself
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי יעקב witnessed this event with his own eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב saw an actual incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this was not a made-up case. רבי יעקב saw it happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because it really happened, the proof stands. A person did both מצוות that promise long life and died right away.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident that took place
He saw

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov saw an incident!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case might be only imagined
steps.terutzMaskana: It truly happened; רבי יעקב saw it

steps.title: Maybe he was thinking about a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the son was punished because he was thinking about doing an עבירה at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he was thinking about a sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another way to explain the death. Maybe the son had sinful thoughts, and that is why he was punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his death was a punishment for something else, it does not show that his מצוה went unrewarded in this world. That would weaken רבי יעקב's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Thinking about, having thoughts of
A sin

phrases.english: But perhaps he was thinking about a sin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the proof after step 9 confirmed the facts
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the death shows the reward was not given in this world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The death could be a punishment for sinful thoughts, not proof that there is no reward

steps.title: ה׳ does not punish bad thoughts as actions
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a rule: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not count a bad thought as if it were a deed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bad thought, הקדוש ברוך הוא does not join it to an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a general rule. A person is not punished just for thinking about a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since thoughts of sin alone are not punished, sinful thoughts cannot explain the son's death. The proof still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad thought, an intention to sin
Joins it to an action, counting it as if it were done

phrases.aramaic: מַחְשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: A bad thought, the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
join it to an action.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He died as punishment for sinful thoughts
steps.terutzMaskana: Bad thoughts alone are not punished, so that cannot explain his death

steps.title: Maybe he was thinking about עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that thoughts of עבודה זרה ARE punished, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל. So maybe that caused his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he was thinking about עבודה זרה, as it says: 'So I may catch the house of Israel in their own heart.' And רב אחא בר יעקב said: this refers to thoughts of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rule from step 11. Thoughts of עבודה זרה are an exception and are punished, so maybe the son was thinking about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that thoughts are not punished has an exception for עבודה זרה, learned from the פסוק. That brings back the possibility that the death was a punishment and not proof against reward in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
The thought of idol worship, which is punished even without action
To catch or grab hold of; here, to hold a person to account

phrases.english: But perhaps he was thinking about idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לְמַעַן תְּפֹשׂ אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלִבָּם״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "So that I may catch the house of Israel in their own heart,"
and Rav Acha bar Ya'akov said:
This is the thought of idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds an exception to the rule in step 11 and renews the challenge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thoughts of עבודה זרה are punished, so the death could still be a punishment

steps.title: If there were reward here, it would have protected him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what רבי יעקב really meant: if מצוות were rewarded in this world, the מצוה would have protected the son from even having such thoughts and being harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if there were reward for מצוות in this world, the מצוה should have helped him and protected him, so that he would not come to such thoughts and be harmed. So there must be no reward for מצוות in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that maybe he had thoughts of עבודה זרה, and still keeps the proof. If reward came in this world, his מצוה should have kept him from those thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is no longer just 'he died, so there was no reward.' Now it is 'a rewarded מצוה would have shielded him from the sin that led to his death.' Since it did not, the reward for מצוות is not given in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means; explains the real point of a statement
Reward for doing מצוות
In this world
It should protect

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב's proof holds even if the son had bad thoughts: a מצוה rewarded in this world would have protected him from them.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that he may have thought about עבודה זרה. It agrees that could be true and shows the proof still works.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יעקב, explaining what he learned from the story he saw.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אִיתָא דְּאִיכָּא שְׂכַר מִצְוֹת בְּהַאי עָלְמָא,
phrases.english: If it were so that there is reward for מצוות in this world,
it should have helped him and protected him
so that he would not come to such thoughts and be harmed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׂכַר מִצְוֹת בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: rather, there is no reward for מצוות in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִם אִיתָא דְּאִיכָּא שְׂכַר מִצְוֹת בְּהַאי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by putting רבי יעקב's reasoning in a sharper way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thoughts of עבודה זרה could explain the death and break the proof
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצוה rewarded in this world would have prevented those thoughts, so there is no reward in this world

steps.title: But those on a מצוה mission are not harmed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from רבי אלעזר: people on their way to do a מצוה are not harmed, so how did this son get hurt?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: שלוחי מצוה are not harmed!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge. רבי אלעזר says a person on a מצוה mission is protected, so the son should not have fallen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not about reward. It is a separate rule of protection while doing a מצוה. The son was sent by his father to do a מצוה, so the rule should have protected him.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say; introduces a challenge from another teaching
People sent to do a מצוה, on a מצוה mission
Harmed, hurt

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
Those on a מצוה mission are not harmed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֵינָן נִזּוֹקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the story itself, from רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that the son died during his מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone on a מצוה mission is protected from harm, so he should not have died

steps.title: On the way back it is different
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the protection is only while going to do the מצוה. The son died on his way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: On their return it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the protection does not cover the trip back. The son fell after he finished the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer limits רבי אלעזר's rule to the way there. Since the son died on the way down, after taking the young birds, the rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: On their return, on the way back
It is different

phrases.english: When they are returning, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The protection covers the whole mission
steps.terutzMaskana: The protection is only on the way to the מצוה, not on the return

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the return is protected too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the fuller version of רבי אלעזר's teaching: שלוחי מצוה are not harmed going OR returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: שלוחי מצוה are not harmed, not on their way there and not on their way back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 15. רבי אלעזר clearly says the protection covers the trip back too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer 'on the way back is different' does not work, because רבי אלעזר's full words include the return. So the question comes back: how could the son die?

keyTerms.meaning: On their way there

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
phrases.notes: It is the same teaching as step 14, now quoted in full with the extra words at the end.

phrases.english: Those on a מצוה mission are not harmed,
neither on their way there nor on their return!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֵינָן נִזּוֹקִים, לֹא בַּהֲלִיכָתָן וְלֹא בַּחֲזָרָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15 using רבי אלעזר's full wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר explicitly includes the return trip in the protection

steps.title: A known danger is different: the shaky ladder
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the son used a rickety ladder. In a place of known danger, even שלוחי מצוה are not protected, as we see from שמואל, who feared שאול would kill him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a rickety ladder, and a place where danger is set is different, as it says: 'And שמואל said: How can I go? If שאול hears, he will kill me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final answer. The protection of שלוחי מצוה does not cover a place of clear, known danger, and a shaky ladder is such a place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule is true, but it has an exception: real, set dangers. The proof is שמואל, who was going on a מצוה from ה׳ and still feared שאול. So the son's death does not go against רבי אלעזר, and רבי יעקב's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A rickety, shaky ladder
A place where danger is set and known

steps.whatToRemember: שלוחי מצוה are protected going and returning, but not in a place of known danger. That is why the son on the shaky ladder could be harmed, and רבי יעקב's proof remains.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of protection for those doing a מצוה: one may not rely on it to walk into a clear danger.

phrases.english: It was a rickety ladder,
and a place where danger is established is different,
as it is written: "And Samuel said: How can I go?
If Saul hears, he will kill me."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:2. שמואל was sent by ה׳ to anoint דוד, and he still feared this danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּלָּם רָעוּעַ הֲוָה, וּמָקוֹם דְּקָבוּעַ הֶיזֵּקָא שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 with an exception to רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception to the rule, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלוחי מצוה are protected in every situation
steps.terutzMaskana: In a place of known danger, like a shaky ladder, the protection does not apply

steps.title: רב יוסף: אחר would not have sinned had he learned the verse like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that if אחר had read the פסוק of reward the way רבי יעקב did, as speaking about עולם הבא, he would not have gone astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If אחר had explained this פסוק the way his daughter's son רבי יעקב did, he would not have sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a new statement. He links רבי יעקב's teaching to the famous sinner אחר, who was רבי יעקב's grandfather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב taught that the promised reward of a long and good life refers to עולם הבא, not this world. רב יוסף says this understanding could have saved אחר. אחר expected reward in this world, and when he did not see it, he lost his faith.

keyTerms.meaning: If only / had it been that
He explained it (as a teaching from the פסוק)
A פסוק, a verse
His daughter's son, his grandson
He sinned

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one wrong reading of a פסוק about reward can shake a person's whole faith.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Had Acher interpreted this verse
phrases.notes: 'This verse' is the promise 'so that it will be good for you and your days will be long,' which רבי יעקב explained earlier.

phrases.english: like Rabbi Yaakov, his daughter's son,
he would not have sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִלְמָלֵא דַּרְשֵׁיהּ אַחֵר לְהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges to רבי יעקב's reading are answered, רב יוסף shows a further consequence of that reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Understanding the reward as belonging to עולם הבא would have kept אחר from sinning.

steps.title: What did אחר see?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what event led אחר to lose his faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. It wants to know what experience pushed אחר away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's statement suggests that אחר saw something that seemed to contradict reward in this world. The גמרא now asks what that event was.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
He saw

phrases.english: What did he see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background behind רב יוסף's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which event caused אחר to doubt that מצוות are rewarded.

steps.title: Two versions of what אחר saw
steps.stepSummary: One version says אחר saw a case like the son who died doing שילוח הקן. Another says he saw the tongue of רבי חוצפית המתורגמן thrown in the garbage, and asked how such a holy mouth could lick the dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he saw an event like this one. Others say he saw the tongue of רבי חוצפית the מתורגמן lying in a garbage heap. He said: Should a mouth that brought out pearls lick the dust?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to what אחר saw. Both are cases where a righteous person seemed to get punishment instead of reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version points back to our story: a son kept two מצוות that promise long life, and he died. The second is the shameful end of רבי חוצפית, whose mouth taught Torah. In both, אחר looked for reward in this world and did not find it.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who announced and explained the רב's lesson to the crowd
A garbage heap
Pearls, here meaning precious words of Torah
Will lick the dust

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: כִּי הַאי מַעֲשֶׂה חֲזָא,
phrases.english: Some say: he saw an incident like this one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the story told earlier: the son climbed to send away the mother bird and fell to his death.

phrases.english: and some say:
he saw the tongue of Rabbi Chutzpit the disseminator,
which was lying in a garbage heap.
He said: A mouth that brought out pearls
should lick the dust?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: כִּי הַאי מַעֲשֶׂה חֲזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what אחר saw.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a case like the son who died doing a מצוה, or the tongue of רבי חוצפית thrown in the garbage.

steps.title: אחר's mistake: the reward is in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what אחר did not understand. 'It will be good for you' means in a world that is all good, and 'your days will be long' means in a world that is all long. That is עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not know that 'so that it will be good for you' means in the world that is entirely good, and 'so that your days will be long' means in the world that is entirely long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the סוגיא by showing where אחר went wrong. The promises of the פסוק are about עולם הבא, not this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What אחר saw only disproves reward in this world. Once the פסוק is read as speaking about עולם הבא, the son's death and רבי חוצפית's end no longer contradict the Torah's promise. This brings us back to רבי יעקב's teaching and seals it.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will be good for you
A world that is entirely good (עולם הבא)
A world that is entirely long, never ending (עולם הבא)

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's promise of 'good' and 'long days' for מצוות like כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן refers to עולם הבא. Suffering in this world does not disprove it. אחר's mistake was expecting the reward here.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the righteous never get good things in this world. It says the promised reward of these פסוקים is measured in עולם הבא, so what happens here cannot disprove it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the closing idea of the מסכת: our view of reward and punishment has to include עולם הבא.

phrases.english: But he did not know
that 'so that it will be good for you' means in the world that is entirely good,
phrases.notes: This promise shows up with כיבוד אב ואם (דברים 5:16) and with שילוח הקן (דברים 22:7).

phrases.english: and 'so that your days will be long'
means in the world that is entirely long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אחר's reasoning from Step 20 and confirms רבי יעקב's reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reward promised in the פסוקים is in עולם הבא, a world entirely good and entirely long.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing פרק שילוח הקן and מסכת חולין
steps.stepSummary: The closing words for פרק שילוח הקן and for the whole of מסכת חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק שילוח הקן, and מסכת חולין is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional הדרן formula. It closes the last פרק and finishes the מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new teaching is added here. Saying 'we will return to you' shows the learner's wish to keep coming back to this Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing formula of a פרק)
Sending away the mother bird from the nest; the name of this פרק
It is finished, completed

steps.whatToRemember: With this, the final פרק, שילוח הקן, and all of מסכת חולין are complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Shiluach HaKen,
and Tractate Chullin is concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing after the sugya's final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק שילוח הקן and of מסכת חולין.
